nc28eaf12de7.s: Under the WTO's Most-Favoured-Nation principle, a customs advantage given to one trading partner must generally be:
o: Extended to all other WTO trading partners
nc28eaf12de7.x: MFN means non-discrimination among trading partners, so an advantage given to one partner must generally go to all other WTO partners, subject to permitted exceptions.

n18cabf95880.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with which objective?
n18cabf95880.x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.

nindian-economy-12-2.s: Which of the following about the WTO is NOT correct?
o: It was established under the Marrakesh Agreement of 1994
It came into being on 1 January 1994
nindian-economy-12-2.x: The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, not 1994, under the Marrakesh Agreement signed in 1994; it replaced the GATT and is headquartered in Geneva.

nindian-economy-12-4.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the GATT is correctly matched?
nindian-economy-12-4.x: The GATT was signed at Geneva on 30 October 1947 by 23 founding contracting parties and came into force in 1948.

n5cef36a18ed.s: The Uruguay Round, launched at Punta del Este in 1986, was which round of GATT negotiations?
n5cef36a18ed.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993 with 123 contracting parties.

n621fe788bfb.s: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals for the agreements of which round of trade negotiations?
n621fe788bfb.x: The Dunkel Draft was made up of proposals by Arthur Dunkel, GATT Director-General and Chair of the Trade Negotiations Committee, for the Uruguay Round agreements.

n22709211653.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MC10 (Nairobi) – Launch of the Doha Development Agenda
MC11 (Buenos Aires) – Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
MC12 (Geneva) – Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
n22709211653.x: The Bali Ministerial Conference (MC9, 2013) produced the Bali Package, including the Trade Facilitation Agreement and an interim Peace Clause on food stockholding.

n0046fdfe8ef.s: At the WTO MC14 at Yaoundé (2026), India blocked the addition of which plurilateral agreement to Annex 4?
n0046fdfe8ef.x: At MC14 India blocked adding the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) plurilateral agreement to Annex 4, although 129 of 166 members backed it.

n5c61c22eae0.s: The Doha Round of WTO negotiations, which remains unfinished, began in:
n5c61c22eae0.x: The Doha Round began in 2001; it deals with agriculture, non-agricultural market access and services and remains unfinished.

nb6be5333423.s: The WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India concerned:
nb6be5333423.x: The sugar dispute concerned India's cane prices and export subsidies; the panel ruled against India in 2021 and the matter was appealed.

n1e4efa65ea3.s: Indian fisher bodies, including Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, have sought which approach to WTO fisheries-subsidy rules?
n1e4efa65ea3.x: The rules matter to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to implementing them.

n977114916fe.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: G-33 – African Group, ACP and LDCs
G-90 – Food security and special products
NAMA-11 – Developing countries on non-agricultural market access
n977114916fe.x: NAMA-11 is a group of developing countries, including India, concerned with non-agricultural market access. The G-90 is the African Group, ACP countries and LDCs.

n765173bfee1.s: Along with IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform, the BRICS New Delhi Declaration (September 2026) sought:
o: Replacement of the WTO by a BRICS trade body
Restoration of the WTO Appellate Body
Merger of the IMF and the World Bank
n765173bfee1.x: The declaration sought IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform and restoration of the two-tier WTO dispute-settlement system, i.e. the Appellate Body.

n9192e4e8e59.s: The WTO Ministerial Conference, its highest decision-making body, must meet at least once every:
n9192e4e8e59.x: Under the Marrakesh Agreement the Ministerial Conference meets at least once every two years.

n276e3416002.s: The G-33, formed in 2003 during the Doha process, mainly focuses on:
o: Interests of the African Group, ACP and LDCs
Food security, Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products
n276e3416002.x: The G-33 is a group of 40-plus developing countries, including India, focused on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.

n695415e97f3.s: India argues that its MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is counted as an Amber Box subsidy using:
n695415e97f3.x: India's public stockholding grievance is that MSP procurement is treated as Amber Box support calculated against an outdated historical reference price.

n379100a2348.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes FDI from FPI?
o: FDI is always debt; FPI is always equity
FDI is regulated only by SEBI; FPI only by the RBI
FDI is generally long-term and may carry management control; FPI is liquid and short-term
FDI is limited to unlisted firms; FPI to government securities
n379100a2348.x: FDI is generally long-term and may bring management control and technology, while FPI is liquid, potentially short-term 'hot money'.

nindian-economy-20-2.s: Which of the following about the SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 is NOT correct?
o: They brought FIIs under the FPI framework
They kept QFIs outside the FPI framework
They brought sub-accounts under the FPI framework
They unified several foreign investor categories as FPIs
nindian-economy-20-2.x: The 2019 Regulations brought FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs together under the FPI framework, so QFIs were not kept outside.

nindian-economy-19-1.s: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is best described as:
o: A short-term domestic loan to Indian enterprises
A largely non-debt, longer-term foreign investment in Indian enterprises
A relatively volatile investment mainly in securities
A government investment made through public expenditure
nindian-economy-19-1.x: FDI is a mostly non-debt capital flow bringing longer-term foreign investment into Indian enterprises; volatile investment in securities is FPI.

nindian-economy-19-8.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wholly owned Indian subsidiary of a foreign company – FPI
Foreign fund buying 5% of a listed Indian company – FDI
nindian-economy-19-8.x: A P-Note is an offshore derivative instrument. A wholly owned subsidiary is FDI, a 5% listed stake is FPI, and a masala bond is a rupee bond issued abroad.

nindian-economy-19-2.s: Which of the following about FDI and FPI is NOT correct?
o: FDI can bring technology and management skills
FDI targets specific sectors or enterprises
FPI is mainly investment in securities
FDI is generally more volatile than FPI
nindian-economy-19-2.x: FDI is more stable and long-term; it is FPI that is the more volatile flow.

n6cb913990d0.s: In India, 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in which e-commerce model?
n6cb913990d0.x: The marketplace model allows 100% FDI through the automatic route; FDI in the inventory model is generally barred, apart from a later export-related relaxation.

n73a7dc952c9.s: Which of the following sector–FDI pairs is correctly matched?
n73a7dc952c9.x: Telecom allows 100% FDI via the automatic route. Single-brand retail is 100% automatic, multi-brand retail 51% Government route, and defence 74% automatic.

n15d20ba35d9.s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, a foreign firm may use the automatic route from 1 May 2026 if its Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership is up to:
n15d20ba35d9.x: Firms with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership up to 10% may use the automatic route, provided they are not registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country.

n7d24366efd1.s: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index, expected to draw passive bond inflows, carries a target weight of:
n7d24366efd1.x: India entered the JP Morgan EM bond index with a target weight of 10%, which is expected to attract passive bond inflows.

na617e27e5a0.s: India opted out of the RCEP in 2019 mainly because of concerns over:
o: The exclusion of ASEAN countries from the bloc
China's market dominance and the widening trade deficit with China
A requirement to withdraw from the WTO
A ban on Indian exports to Australia
na617e27e5a0.x: India withdrew over China's market dominance, its rising trade deficit with China and risks to farm, dairy and small industries.

na81c5c76d18.s: The Andhra Pradesh Mutually Aided Cooperative Societies (MACS) Act was enacted in:
na81c5c76d18.x: The AP MACS Act dates from 1995; the AP Cooperative Societies Act dates from 1964.

nindian-economy-2-4.s: Which of the following institution–year of establishment pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-economy-2-4.x: IDBI was set up in 1964. IFCI dates from 1948, ICICI from 1955 and SIDBI from 1990.

ne476f862410.s: The National Housing Bank, wholly owned by the RBI until then, was taken over by the Central Government in:
ne476f862410.x: NHB was set up in 1988 and stayed wholly RBI-owned until the Central Government took over its ownership in 2019.

n0b7f6600d66.s: After the IL&FS defaults, the Government superseded the company's board through an order of the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
n0b7f6600d66.x: Following the IL&FS defaults, the Government superseded its board through an NCLT order.

n4cb12082059.s: Which of the following about reserve requirements is NOT correct?
n4cb12082059.x: NBFCs do not maintain CRR; banks maintain CRR and SLR, while deposit-taking NBFCs maintain liquid assets instead. (Restyled from a one-best-statement form to NOT.)

nedf5b2f5564.s: Under Scale-Based Regulation, an NBFC identified by the RBI for the Upper Layer must get listed within:
nedf5b2f5564.x: Upper Layer NBFCs are identified by the RBI, follow bank-like norms for at least five years and must list within three years.

n1d75f7dcb1b.s: State Cooperative Banks and DCCBs are licensed by the RBI and inspected by:
o: The State Registrar of Cooperative Societies
n1d75f7dcb1b.x: StCBs and DCCBs are licensed by the RBI and inspected by NABARD, while PACS fall under State Registrars.

n9a03b868e8c.s: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), funded by banks' priority-sector lending shortfalls, is managed by:
n9a03b868e8c.x: NABARD manages RIDF, which is funded by banks' PSL shortfalls; it also refinances StCBs, RRBs and land development banks.

n18b4bad8f5d.s: The Microfinance Industry Network (MFIN), the association of NBFC-MFIs, was set up in:
n18b4bad8f5d.x: MFIN was set up in 2009; the RBI recognised it as a self-regulatory organisation in 2014.

nc4462c33c16.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Nationalisation of the RBI
2. Appointment of the Hilton Young Commission
3. Passing of the RBI Act
4. RBI starts functioning
nc4462c33c16.x: Hilton Young Commission (1926), RBI Act (1934), RBI begins operations (1935), nationalisation (1949).

nindian-economy-8-1.s: The Reserve Bank of India began functioning on:
nindian-economy-8-1.x: The RBI began work on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934; it was nationalised with effect from 1 January 1949.

nindian-economy-8-2.s: Which of the following about the Reserve Bank of India is NOT correct?
o: It was originally headquartered in Kolkata
It became fully government-owned after nationalisation
Its head office is now in Mumbai
nindian-economy-8-2.x: The RBI was nationalised in 1949, not 1937; 1937 is when its head office moved from Kolkata to Mumbai.

n23721c2c6f3.s: Who was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
n23721c2c6f3.x: C. D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor of the RBI, serving from 1943 to 1949.

n17b1273a2c6.s: Who was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
n17b1273a2c6.x: Sir Osborne Smith was the first RBI Governor (1935-37); he signed no Indian note because King Edward VIII had abdicated.

nccf7349d88c.s: Who has been the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India since December 2024?
nccf7349d88c.x: Sanjay Malhotra has been RBI Governor since December 2024 and chairs the MPC and the Payments Regulatory Board; Shaktikanta Das was Governor 2018-2024.

n8f742a42260.s: Under Section 7 of the RBI Act, the Central Government may give directions to the RBI in the public interest after consulting the:
n8f742a42260.x: Section 7 allows the Central Government to issue directions to the RBI in the public interest after consulting the RBI Governor.

nindian-economy-8-4.s: Which of the following pairs of RBI function and role is correctly matched?
o: Controller of credit – Controls money and credit through monetary policy
Banker to Government – Oversight of payment systems
Payment systems – Management of foreign exchange reserves
nindian-economy-8-4.x: As controller of credit the RBI runs monetary policy. As banker to Government it handles transactions and public debt; it also manages forex reserves and oversees payment systems.

n0a488c6fcae.s: The ₹2,000 note, withdrawn from circulation in May 2023:
o: Ceased to be legal tender immediately
Is legal tender only for banks
n0a488c6fcae.x: The ₹2,000 note was withdrawn from circulation in May 2023 but continues to have legal-tender status.

nindian-economy-8-10.s: In India, the ₹1 note is issued by:
o: The Government of India (Ministry of Finance)
nindian-economy-8-10.x: The ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India through the Ministry of Finance, which also issues coins; the RBI issues the other notes.

nindian-economy-41-4.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SLR – Reserve maintained with the RBI
CRR – Liquid assets held by the bank itself
Increase in SLR – Reduces investible loan funds
Decrease in SLR – Reduces investible loan funds
nindian-economy-41-4.x: Raising SLR locks more funds in liquid assets and cuts loanable funds. SLR is held by the bank itself, CRR with the RBI, and an SLR cut frees funds.

nindian-economy-38-1.s: Which is the most commonly used measure of broad money supply in India?
nindian-economy-38-1.x: M3 (broad money) is the most used measure; M1 is narrow money and M0 is reserve money.

nindian-economy-38-2.s: Which of the following about money supply measures is NOT correct?
o: M1 includes currency with the public
Other deposits with the RBI are part of both M1 and M3
Time deposits with banks are part of M1
M3 includes time deposits with banks
nindian-economy-38-2.x: Time deposits are not part of M1 (currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits); they are included in M3.

n1d7cbfa931f.s: Deposit money, created by lending beyond required reserves, is created mainly by:
n1d7cbfa931f.x: The RBI creates reserve money by issuing notes, while commercial banks create deposit money by lending beyond their required CRR and SLR reserves.

n3fc4f1a1d28.s: If money supply is fixed and the demand for money rises, the interest rate will:
n3fc4f1a1d28.x: With a fixed money supply, a rise in money demand raises the interest rate; a fall in demand lowers it.

n8e5a32879cd.s: 'Hard money' refers to money backed by:
n8e5a32879cd.x: Hard money is backed by gold or credible assets; soft money is paper money backed by government bonds.

neb6f4406613.s: Which ratio is maintained by banks as a cash balance with the RBI and earns no interest?
neb6f4406613.x: CRR is kept as a cash balance with the RBI and earns no interest; SLR is held by the bank itself in cash, gold and eligible securities.

nindian-economy-9-1.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bank Rate – RBI absorbs liquidity from banks
Repo Rate – RBI buys or sells government securities
Reverse Repo – RBI lends to banks against securities
OMO – RBI buys or sells government securities
nindian-economy-9-1.x: OMO is the RBI buying or selling government securities. Bank rate is its lending rate, repo is lending against securities and reverse repo absorbs liquidity.

nindian-economy-40-2.s: Which of the following about the Reverse Repo is NOT correct?
o: It is a monetary policy tool
It is used to absorb surplus liquidity
Under it, banks borrow from the RBI
Under it, the RBI borrows from banks
nindian-economy-40-2.x: Under reverse repo the RBI borrows from banks to absorb surplus liquidity; banks borrowing from the RBI is repo.

n15c8a60fe21.s: The SLR, which was 38.5 per cent in 1991–92, stood at what level in September 2023?
n15c8a60fe21.x: The SLR was 18 per cent in September 2023, down from 38.5 per cent in 1991–92.

na9d1bd31b97.s: India's flexible inflation-targeting framework is based on the recommendations of which committee?
na9d1bd31b97.x: The Urjit Patel Committee reported in 2014, the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement followed in 2015 and the RBI Act was amended in 2016.

nindian-economy-42-2.s: Which of the following about the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) is NOT correct?
o: It is an overnight borrowing facility
Banks borrow from the RBI under it
Its rate is lower than the repo rate
Its rate is usually repo plus 0.25%
nindian-economy-42-2.x: MSF costs more than repo, usually repo plus 0.25%; it is an overnight emergency window, while repo is for regular liquidity.

n471bf2d1fcb.s: The Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS), introduced in April 2004, was meant to:
o: Sterilise excess liquidity created by foreign-exchange purchases
Replace the repo for daily liquidity adjustment
n471bf2d1fcb.x: Under the MSS the RBI issues Treasury Bills and securities to absorb rupees created by forex purchases; the proceeds sit in a separate account the Government cannot spend.

n971c011763f.s: The decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee are:
o: Advisory and not binding on the RBI
Subject to approval by the RBI Central Board
n971c011763f.x: MPC decisions are binding on the RBI; the inflation target itself is set by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI.

n898c8a0ac3f.s: Which inflation-target notification – period covered pair is correctly matched?
n898c8a0ac3f.x: The 25 March 2026 notification covers April 2026–March 2031; the August 2016 one covered up to March 2021 and the March 2021 one April 2021–March 2026.

n61bc54a06e7.s: In April 2025, when the repo rate was cut to 6 per cent, the RBI's monetary-policy stance moved from neutral to:
n61bc54a06e7.x: The stance moved from neutral to accommodative in April 2025 with the cut to 6 per cent; it was neutral in 2026 when the repo rate was held at 5.25 per cent.

n753b7a0039b.s: The new CPI-Combined series released by the NSO (MoSPI) in February 2026 has the base year:
n753b7a0039b.x: CPI-Combined, the nominal anchor for the inflation target, is compiled by the NSO under MoSPI; the new series of 12 February 2026 has base year 2024 (earlier 2012).

n8396e51401e.s: The failure clause under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework was first invoked in:
n8396e51401e.x: The failure clause was first invoked in 2022; March 2026 marked the second retention of the original target.

n58c79bbf809.s: Andhra Bank, founded at Machilipatnam in 1923 by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya, was merged in 2020 into:
n58c79bbf809.x: Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India in 2020; Indian Bank absorbed Allahabad Bank.

nindian-economy-2-2.s: Which of the following about SBI and Regional Rural Banks is NOT correct?
o: SBI was formed from the Imperial Bank of India
Prathama Grameen Bank was the first RRB
The first RRB was set up on 2 October 1974
nindian-economy-2-2.x: The first RRB, Prathama Grameen Bank, opened on 2 October 1975, not 1974.

nindian-economy-30-2.s: The Life Insurance Corporation of India was formed under the LIC Act, 1956 on:
nindian-economy-30-2.x: LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 by merging over 240 insurers and societies; 19 July 1969 is when 14 banks were nationalised.

nc2954590716.s: The setting up of Regional Rural Banks in 1975 was recommended by the:
nc2954590716.x: The Narasimham Working Group recommended RRBs in 1975; Prathama Grameen Bank was the first RRB.

n727da463764.s: The shareholding of a Regional Rural Bank among the Centre, the State Government and the sponsor bank is:
n727da463764.x: RRBs follow a 50:15:35 shareholding among the Central Government, State Government and sponsor bank.

n908a4bc6efc.s: Regional Rural Banks are regulated by the RBI and supervised by:
n908a4bc6efc.x: RRBs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India and supervised by NABARD.

nindian-economy-2-7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Location of the first RRB – Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
nindian-economy-2-7.x: The first RRB was set up at Moradabad (UP); banks were nationalised first in 1969 and again in 1980.

nbf9884b7a13.s: The Imperial Bank of India was formed by merging:
o: Punjab National Bank, Allahabad Bank and Canara Bank
Awadh Commercial Bank and Punjab National Bank
nbf9884b7a13.x: The Imperial Bank of India was formed by merging the three Presidency banks.

n8a8c0d2ce0b.s: Bank loans to micro and small enterprises must be given without collateral up to:
n8a8c0d2ce0b.x: MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh and all PMEGP units must be collateral-free; banks may raise this limit to ₹25 lakh.

n9346d3c5132.s: Basel I (1988), which focused on credit risk, prescribed minimum capital of what share of risk-weighted assets?
n9346d3c5132.x: Basel I addressed credit risk and set minimum capital at 8 per cent of risk-weighted assets (India prescribed 9 per cent).

n689e88c28f4.s: Which of the following may be included in a bank's Tier 2 capital?
n689e88c28f4.x: Tier 2 has a mixed equity-debt character and may include subordinated debt; paid-up capital, reserves and undistributed profits are Tier 1 core equity.

n42745014d94.s: The countercyclical capital buffer, introduced in India in 2015 but not yet activated, allows extra capital during credit booms in the range of:
n42745014d94.x: The CCyB ranges from 0 to 2.5 per cent during credit booms; India has had the framework since 2015 but has not activated it.

ne9444f5029b.s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
ne9444f5029b.x: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.

nindian-economy-30-20.s: The merger of Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank into Bank of Baroda took effect on:
nindian-economy-30-20.x: The Bank of Baroda merger took effect on 1 April 2019; the 2020 mergers took effect on 1 April 2020 and the SBI merger on 1 April 2017.

ncd9845bef2c.s: After the 2020–21 consolidation, the number of Regional Rural Banks (originally 196) came down to:
ncd9845bef2c.x: There were originally 196 RRBs; the 2020–21 consolidation brought the number down to 43.

neb85b1bff8e.s: Which of the following asset classifications is correctly matched?
o: Standard asset – NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset – NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset – NPA for 12 months or less
neb85b1bff8e.x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for 12 months or less; an NPA for more than 12 months is doubtful.

n053d18a30a0.s: A loan for a short-duration crop becomes an NPA when it remains overdue for:
n053d18a30a0.x: Agricultural loans become NPAs after two crop seasons for short-duration crops and one crop season for long-duration crops.
